data.title: Cetirizine
data.summary: IX Antihistaminics · Second-generation H1 antihistamine (piperazine; carboxylic acid metabolite of hydroxyzine)
data.body:
_Oral · IX Antihistaminics_

**Class:** Second-generation H1 antihistamine (piperazine; carboxylic acid metabolite of hydroxyzine)

## Mechanism of action
- Selective peripheral H1 inverse agonist
- Some anti-inflammatory effect: reduces eosinophil migration and late-phase reactions

## Pharmacokinetics
- Rapid onset (within 1 h); half-life about 8–10 h; once daily
- Excreted mostly unchanged in urine — halve the dose in renal impairment
- Levocetirizine is the active R-enantiomer (5 mg = 10 mg cetirizine)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic spontaneous and inducible urticaria (first line)
- Allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis itch (limited), insect bite reactions, mastocytosis

## Dose & formulations
- Adults: 10 mg once daily; in urticaria may be increased up to 4 times (40 mg/day) per guidelines
- Children 6 months–2 years: 2.5 mg daily; 2–6 years: 2.5 mg twice daily or 5 mg daily; over 6 years: 10 mg daily

## Adverse effects
- Mild sedation (more than fexofenadine and loratadine; about 10%)
- Headache, dry mouth, fatigue

## Contraindications
- Severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance under 10 mL/min)
- Hypersensitivity to hydroxyzine or piperazines

## Drug interactions
- Alcohol and CNS depressants (mild additive effect)

## Monitoring
- None

## Pregnancy & lactation
One of the preferred antihistamines in pregnancy (with loratadine); compatible with breastfeeding (watch infant drowsiness).

## Viva points
- Metabolite of hydroxyzine
- Renally excreted — adjust in kidney disease
- Most sedating of the second-generation group
- Updosing up to 4 times in urticaria

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.32; Khopkar (Antihistamines). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
